---
title: "CATLAS"
subtitle: "**C**onditioning **A**s a **T**heory of **L**earned **A**ttention, **S**emantics and more"
---

CATLAS is a research program on associative learning theories of attention
and schema induction. Its aim is to develop and evaluate theoretical and
computational accounts of how learned associations shape attentional
allocation and the acquisition of structured knowledge.

This site publishes the manuscripts of the program together with the analysis
notebooks behind them. Every page is rendered from the
[CATLAS repository](https://github.com/josefmana/CATLAS), where its source
lives.

## Manuscripts

**[Disentangling Attentional Shift and Attentional Competition Accounts of
Associative Blocking](forward-blocking-attention-01/index.html)**\
Replication and extension of Beesley & Le Pelley
([2011](https://doi.org/10.1037/a0019526)). In preparation; the
pre-registration of Experiment 1 is among its notebooks.

## Related repositories

- [`{catlasr}`](https://josefmana.github.io/catlasr/): the R package for
  importing, validating, scoring and sharing the data of CATLAS studies.
- [`catlaslab`](https://github.com/josefmana/catlaslab): the experiments
  (jsPsych on JATOS), with every deployed build attached to a release.
- [`{mathpsychr}`](https://github.com/josefmana/mathpsychr): theory-agnostic
  mathematical psychology machinery in R.
